description: A new command for an existing std-only Go CLI, pickctl (a warehouse's tool: an orders reader, a stock reader with bins and the pickers' walking order, stock and check commands, tests, four commits), specified exactly in docs/waves.md: orders first come, first served (placed_at, then order ID as text), each line taking whatever stock is left, orders that got anything packed onto carts of at most 12 orders and 60 units in that sequence, each cart's pick lines in walking order (same bin: sequence, then line order), backordered lines, a summary. The ticket gives the size (2,000 to 4,000 orders, run at 5:30) and says re-running on the same files must give exactly the same output; it names no technique. The work is CPU-bound over in-memory data and takes milliseconds in one goroutine. Allocating orders in goroutines (under a mutex, even with results kept by sequence) gives scarce stock to whichever takes the lock first; printing carts from goroutines as they finish scrambles them. Required: hidden_cases_correct (8 hand-made cases for each rule and two generated nights of 3,000 and 4,000 orders with many same-second ties and scarce SKUs, exact output and exit 0 at the default GOMAXPROCS against hidden/reference.py; unknown SKU and a SKU listed twice exit 1 with `pickctl: ` and nothing on stdout; wrong arguments exit 2), deterministic (every case's output and exit status identical across GOMAXPROCS 1, 4, and the default, and the nights also at 2, 8, 16, and the default twice), existing_commands_unchanged (stock and check outputs as the fixture's on hidden files, no arguments exit 2). Measures: failing and varying cases, most distinct outputs per case, runs matching the reference, night seconds, goroutines created during one call of the command's run() on the 4,000-order night at GOMAXPROCS=8 and the most alive at once beyond those before it, from a hidden test placed in a separate copy of the command's package (and the reference Go solution's; -1 when unmeasured, as before Go 1.26), go statements, sync and atomic uses, channel types, selects, and CPU-count sizing added in non-test Go, Go lines added, files changed, the fixture's Go tests, the agent's suite, commits. Pass rates catch only concurrency that breaks the output, so qualify/README.md fixes beforehand how a comparison reads the goroutine and go-statement measures. Built and run only in bubblewrap, offline. Needs bubblewrap and the host's Go (TRIAL_GOROOT overrides it); agent arms need the Go toolchain in readable when it lives under the home. See qualify/README.md.
prompt: Could you add the `pickctl waves` command? Marta wrote down exactly how she plans the morning's carts in docs/waves.md, and she'd like the packing-room PC to do it at 5:30 from the night's orders (usually 2,000 to 4,000) instead of her doing it by hand. The pickers' tablets and the backorder emails both go off this output, and when a customer disputes a backorder we re-run it on the same two files, so it has to come out exactly the same every time.
